paper_title: Increasing the Effectiveness of Automatically Generated Tests by Improving Class Observability

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: Increasing class observability through injected public accessors and recursive assertions significantly increases generated tests' mutation scores.
claims.evidence_quote: our evaluation demonstrates that together these observability improvements lead to significantly increased mutation scores

claims.statement: Injecting public accessors for private/protected attributes significantly increases average mutation score in 26 of the 57 classes that use those injected getters in generated assertions.
claims.evidence_quote: 26 of these 57 classes have a significant increase in their average mutation score when using injected getters.

claims.statement: Mutation score improvements from injected getters range from 0.13% to 49% across the 26 significantly improved classes.
claims.evidence_quote: improved their mutation score from 0.13% to 49%

claims.statement: Recursive assertions on composed objects add limited additional benefit beyond injected getters, with a maximum increase of 21.13% in one class and an average increase of only 0.30% among the other classes.
claims.evidence_quote: the addition of recursive assertions raised the mutation score by a maximum of 21.13% in the NotificationEventComparator class. However, this addition did not increase the mutation score of the other classes, which has an average increase of 0.30% on the mutation score.

claims.statement: In the combined recursive assertions condition, 26 classes showed statistically significant mutation score improvements, with improvements ranging from 0.6% to 49%.
claims.evidence_quote: The increment on mutation score in these classes ranges from 0.6% to 49% and a maximum of 51 new mutants were detected.

overall_conclusion: Improving class observability in EvoSuite by injecting public accessors for private/protected attributes and enabling recursive assertions on complex object state significantly improves generated tests' mutation scores for a subset of classes. The injected getters provide the main benefit, while recursive assertions add only limited further improvement.
comparable_notes: Evaluation used 100 SF110 Java classes filtered by cyclomatic complexity threshold of 3, with EvoSuite/DynaMOSA as baseline. Test generation used 30 seeds per class, producing 12,000 test suites total. Comparison used one-tailed Wilcoxon tests at alpha=0.05 and Vargha-Delaney A12 effect sizes. Injected accessors and recursive assertions were excluded from test goals and mutation score computation. Mutation score was measured over 26,177 total generated mutants.
